title: Scaling AI in Education: A Khanmigo case study: Shawn Jansepar
talk_summary: Shawn Jansepar describes how Khan Academy built Khanmigo, an AI tutor, by pairing builders with domain experts, using demo-driven rapid prototyping, and creating an AI platform team that owns shared components like an AI router and tracing. Technically they improved math accuracy with a math agent, chain-of-thought prompting, and a tutoring accuracy dashboard, while managing cost and reliability through multi-model routing, fallback to shared capacity, and model-graded evals.

takeaways.technique: Multi-model routing with fallback to shared capacity
takeaways.what_they_do: They use multiple models in production for different workflows and fall back to shared capacity when dedicated capacity limits are reached, with an AI platform team owning the router so product teams don't worry about it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: leveraging multiple models in production for different workflows uh fall back to Shared capacity when we're reaching limits on our dedicated capacity

takeaways.technique: Tutoring accuracy dashboard and regression monitoring
takeaways.what_they_do: They built a dashboard to monitor quality over time so that prompt changes and model upgrades don't cause regressions, and they are building a math accuracy benchmark dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: building this tutoring accuracy dashboard monitor uh to monitor quality over time so we can kind of get a sense of as we're shipping new changes
takeaways.numbers: Model-graded evals catch math mistakes ~70% of the time vs human labels

takeaways.technique: Chain-of-thought decomposition before the final call
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of one prompt, they first ask the model to write out how the student likely arrived at the answer and how it should have, then feed that package into a second call that does the tutoring.
takeaways.evidence_quote: write out how a how you think the student might have arrived at that answer write out how you think it should have arrived at that answer and then it kind of feeds that package over to another call

takeaways.technique: Specialist math agent with tool access
takeaways.what_they_do: They give the main AI autonomy to defer to a math agent that can use a calculator or Python for harder problems rather than doing all reasoning in one model.
takeaways.evidence_quote: introduced a math agent so we kind of give the AI the autonomy to defer to a math agent to work through problems

takeaways.technique: Component interface enforcing tracing and testability
takeaways.what_they_do: An AI platform team built a Go component interface; conforming to it automatically gives tracing and Langfuse, and clearly defined inputs/outputs make sub-pieces easier to test.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when you as a developer conform to that component interface it automatically think means that things like tracing and Lang fuse are available

takeaways.what_they_do: They replaced heavyweight agile with a process where code quality bar scales with confidence: scrappy for prototypes, beta for somewhat confident, full checklists only when shipping to all users.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's a different level of quality of your code that you should write depending on your confidence in the fature
